General Plan/LCP FEIR Conclusions
The 2030 GP/LCP would facilitate the development of Expansion Areas No. 1, 2, and 3, as well as
intensified development throughout the City, especially in the City Center and the Avalon Canyon
areas. Intensified development would be located within the existing Avalon Fire Department service
area and the existing response times would apply. As such, the intensification of development
within the City would not require new or expanded fire or emergency service facilities because
they would fall within the existing service area and response times. However, the expansion areas
would increase the service area, which may also increase response times. Avalon Fire Department
response times to any new development within expansion areas may be greater than for the areas
within the current City limits. However, all three expansion areas would still be expected to fall
within a 5-minute response area. While fire and emergency medical service capacity is primarily
based on service area, an increase in population would incrementally increase the number of
service calls and would eventually necessitate the need for additional staff and facilities. However,
new development would be required to comply with any additional project-specific requirements
set forth by the Avalon Fire Department, including providing adequate water pressure and water
for fire flows. In addition to property taxes, which supports the Avalon Fire Department, the City
can also require mitigation fees as a condition of approval for individual projects to ensure that
new developments contribute a fair share to fire and emergency services, facilities, and
infrastructure. In addition, new development sited in high fire hazard areas would be required to
adhere to standard requirements set forth by the California Building Code (CBC) with City of Avalon
  Environmental Analysis  4-44
   City of Avalon I 2021-2029 Housing Element Update
  Addendum to the General Plan/LCP FEIR

amendments. The entire City is designated as a very high fire hazard zone. Therefore, any
development in the City would be sited in very high fire hazard zones and would be required to
adhere to applicable policies. Any development in hillside areas is of particular concern because
these areas are especially fire prone. Adherence to standard requirements would minimize the
risks of fire hazards. Further, the 2030 GP/LCP contains policies aimed at addressing potential
wild fire hazards associated with potential new development. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR
concluded that development facilitated by the 2030 GP/LCP would not result in the need for new
or expanded fire protection facilities and impacts relating to fire protection would be less than
significant.

Police protection services are not “facility-driven;” that is, police protection services are not as
reliant on facilities in order to effectively patrol a beat. An expansion of, or intensification of
development within, a beat does not necessarily result in the need for additional facilities if police
officers and patrol vehicles are equipped with adequate telecommunications equipment in order to
communicate with police headquarters. However, if the geographical area of a beat is expanded,
population increases, or intensification/redevelopment of an existing beat results in the need for
new police officers, new or expanded facilities could be needed. The Avalon Patrol Station provides
police protection services within the City and would continue to provide police protection services
through 2030. Development facilitated by the 2030 GP/LCP would not result in the need to
construct new police facilities and there would only be a slight increase, if any, in the response
times for the potential expansion areas. While the response times would remain relatively low, the
projected increase in population through the year 2030 could increase the demand for additional
sworn officers. In the event that additional officers are needed to provide adequate police services,
the City’s General Fund would continue to provide the finances necessary to employ additional
officers. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that development facilitated by the 2030
GP/LCP would not result in the need for new or expanded police protection facilities and impacts
would be less than significant.

Development facilitated by the 2030 GP/LCP would likely increase enrollment at Avalon Schools.
The General Plan/LCP concluded that new students potentially generated by future development
facilitated by the 2030 GP/LCP would not exceed the current capacity. State-mandated school
impact fees would, however, be required for any new development projects. Pursuant to Section
65995(h) of the California Government Code (Senate Bill 50, chaptered August 27, 1998), the
payment of statutory fees  “.  is deemed to be full and complete mitigation of the impacts of any
legislative or adjudicative act, or both, involving, but not limited to, the planning, use, or
development of real property, or any change in governmental organization or reorganization.”
Because existing school facilities are sufficient to serve the existing population and the anticipated
growth, expansion or construction of new facilities are not planned at this time. The remaining
available capacity of Avalon School and future payments of school impact fees would ensure that
impacts to schools would be less than significant. Site- and project-specific environmental review
would be required for schools if, or when, new sites are proposed for development in the future.
Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that the collection of State-mandated school
impact fees would reduce school capacity impacts to a less than significant level.

Development facilitated by the 2030 GP/LCP would likely generate increased demand for harbor

General Plan/LCP PEER Conclusions
Avalon does not contain any roadways that are part of the 2010 Los Angeles Congestion
Management Plan Transit Network. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP concluded that the 2030
GP/LCP would not conflict with the applicable congestion management plan and no impact would
occur in this regard. Though there is an airfield on the northern part of Catalina Island, there are
no airfields or airports within the City of Avalon. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP concluded that
no impact to air traffic patterns would occur as a result of buildout under the 2030 GP/LCP.

The 2030 GP/LCP would facilitate development of expansion areas and intensify development in
Avalon Canyon. This may incrementally increase traffic on Avalon’s roadway system and affect
both intersections and roadway capacities. Avalon does not currently use level of service or other
standards for pedestrian and vehicular circulation; rather, the City strictly regulates vehicle use.
According to the 2006 Facilities and Services Holding Capacity Report for the City ofAvalon, overall,
there is 46°/o of total vehicle capacity remaining. It is expected that residential and commercial
vehicle use would remain constant or drop over time, but the use of autoettes (smaller vehicles
with higher fuel efficiency) would increase as more housing units are developed. Assuming a 1 to
1 ratio of housing units to new autoettes, autoette usage would increase by 22°/o, which is within
the remaining vehicle capacity of 46w/a. In addition, the 2030 GP/LCP identifies physical and
operational improvements that would address existing circulation issues and accommodate growth.
Further, the 2030 GP/LCP includes policies and actions specifically intended to accommodate traffic
generated by new growth in the City. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that

adherence to GP/LCP policies and implementation of planned improvements would ensure the
roadway network in Avalon does not exceed capacity and impacts would be less than significant.

The 2030 GP/LCP encourages higher-density, mixed-use mull in the City Center. By emphasizing
 intensification and reuse in the City Center, the GP/LCP could accommodate new mixed use and
residential development along existing roadways. The placement of residences along existing
travel corridors is expected to generally increase bicycling and pedestrian activity in these areas,
with the potential for increased hazards for pedestrians and bicyclists. However, the 2030 GP/LCP
includes policies and actions specifically intended to increase traffic calming and enhance the
walkability throughout the City. By designating appropriate street segments as one-way and
closing appropriate segments to through traffic, friction between pedestrians, bicyclists, and
vehicles would be reduced. Implementation of proposed policies is expected to generally improve
overall safety conditions for pedestrians throughout the City. Implementation of GP/LCP policies
on any future development would also minimize traffic-related hazards associated with the
development of those areas. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that impacts related
to traffic safety as a result of development under the 2030 GP/LCP would be less than significant.

A goal of the 2030 GP/LCP is to “reduce the amount that people drive by increasing opportunities
for walking, bicycling, and transit.” The 2030 GP/LCP includes policies aimed at enhancement of
alternative transportation mode opportunities throughout the City. In addition, the GP/LCP
emphasizes intensification and reuse of already developed areas of the City. Implementation of
the policies included in the 2030 GP/LCP is expected to improve the availability of sidewalks, bike
paths, and transit over time. Planned improvements in the Circulation Element would improve
alternative transportation modes. By making these transportation alternatives more attractive,
GP/LCP implementation is expected to foster an increase of alternative transportation use and a
decrease of vehicle use. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that impacts related to
alternative transportation would be considered beneficial.

As described above, areas within one-mile beyond the existing city limits would be within the
Avalon Fire Department’s 5-minute response area. In addition, all three expansion areas would
still be expected to fall within a 5-minute response area. However, the 2030 GP/LCP would facilitate
development into Expansion Areas and into hillside areas that are currently not served by roads,
or are served by one roadway. Currently, the Hamilton Cove area is only accessible through one
road, which is prone to rock slides. During an emergency event, a slide could prevent emergency
access to this area. Improvements in this area are already partially funded and underway.
Development facilitated by the proposed 2030 GP/LCP would be required to comply with applicable
Building Code and Fire Code requirements. As such, new development would also be required to
comply with any additional project-specific requirements set forth by the Avalon Fire Department,
including providing adequate emergency access. In addition, the 2030 GP/LCP includes policies
consistent with this requirement. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that
implementation of the 2030 GP/LCP policies and compliance with existing building and fire codes
would address potential emergency access issues associated with potential new development and
impacts would be less than significant.

General Plan/LCP FEIR Conclusions
Development facilitated by the 2030 GP/LCP includes development and redevelopment of lands
within the current City boundaries, as well as within potential annexation areas, referred to as
“Expansion Areas.” Areas where redevelopment activity could occur include areas that are already
served by existing water infrastructure. Development of vacant lands would require new
connections. New development would result in a permanent increase in the City’s water demand
relative to existing conditions. The General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that current surplus of
freshwater would be adequate to serve the estimated increase in demand due to the 2030 GP/LCP.
In addition, the desalination plant has the capacity to increase the production of desalinated water,
which would provide an additional buffer of freshwater availability for growth projected under the
2030 GP/LCP. Further, infrastructure improvements and increased connectivity to the saltwater
system would further reduce demand on freshwater. Due to the limited groundwater supply in
Avalon and the high cost of desalinated water, the City should continue to pursue new sources of

  Addendum to the General Plan/LCP FEIR

freshwater and implement water conservation strategies. Accordingly, the 2030 GP/LCP contains
policies that would further reduce impacts to water supply. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR
concluded that water supply impacts would be less than significant.

Population growth projected under the 2030 GP/LCP would increase city-wide wastewater
generation. However, sufficient treatment capacity exists at the Avalon Wastewater Treatment
Facility to serve the increase in population under the 2030 GP/LCP. In addition, sewer line capacity
estimates indicate that there is sufficient capacity to accommodate existing and new wastewater
generated by additional population under the 2030 GP/LCP. Further, the City’s Municipal Code
requires all plans for the construction of sewer infrastructure to meet all design requirements, as
established by the City Engineer. Projects that could occur during the lifetime of the 2030 GP/LCP
would be examined on an individual basis to determine their effects on the wastewater
infrastructure. Therefore, the General Plan/LCP FEIR concluded that with adherence to the City’s
Municipal Code and because the wastewater treatment provider has adequate capacity to meet
the potential population growth, no new wastewater treatment facilities or the expansion of
existing facilities would be necessary, and impacts related to the City’s sewer system capacity
would be less than significant.

Increased population and development that may occur under the GP/LCP would generate additional
solid waste. The General Plan/LCP concluded that the Pebbly Beach Disposal site would have
sufficient capacity to serve the daily throughput of solid waste generated by the 2030 population.
In addition, the City has entered into a new contract with CR&R, Inc that would extend the capacity
and life of the landfill. Under this new disposal agreement with CR&R, the life and capacity of the
landfill would be extended to the year 2033 on account of a larger baler that would be installed at
the landfill site. Additionally, the height of the landfill would be raised and an energy to power
plant is being proposed that would further extend the life of the landfill. Further, the City has
implemented 25 diversion programs to increase the life of the landfill. The California Integrated
Waste Management Act of 1989 requires all cities in California to achieve a 50°/o solid waste
diversion rate by the year 2000. As of 2006, the City of Avalon achieved a solid waste diversion
rate of 7O%. In addition to the diversion programs in place, the 2030 GP/LCP includes policies and
implementation actions related to minimizing solid waste. Potential future development facilitated
by the 2030 GP/LCP would also be reviewed on a project-by-project basis; solid waste impacts
would be evaluated based on existing and planned disposal facilities and capacities available.
Therefore, the General Plan/LCP concluded that through the continued efforts of the existing
diversion programs and the new disposal agreement with CR&R that would extend the life and
capacity of the landfill through at least the year 2033, the GP/LCP policies and implementation
actions, and project specific review, the current landfill facility would have sufficient capacity to
serve the daily throughput of solid waste generated by the 2030 population; impacts related to
solid waste would be less than significant.

SUBJECT:  First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Chapter 5-101 of Title 5
  of the Avalon Municipal Code Relating to Advertising Matter and
  Posting on Public Property

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Introduce and waive all readings of an ordinance of the City of
Avalon amending Chapter 5-1.01 of Title 5 of the Avalon Municipal Code Relating to
Advertising Matter and Posting on Public Property.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City’s temporary banner permit policy was established by
Ordinance Number 759 in 1984. The ordinance allowed banners to be strung across the public
rights-of-way for a period of no more than seven (7) days.

In 2009, this timeframe was extended to “no more than 42 days (6 weeks) preceding the event
it is advertising, and shall be removed no more than three (3) days after the event it is
advertising,” by Ordinance Number 1085-09.

City Staff recommend amending this portion of the ordinance again to read: “The sign shall be
posted in one location for no more than 42 days (six weeks). The permit shall contain a
statement to this effect which must be signed by the applicant.”

Additionally, City Staff recommends establishing a maximum banner size of tour (4) feet by
twelve (12) feet.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: n/a

FISCAL IMPACTS: There is no fiscal impact associated with the recommended action.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The temporary banner
permit policy will remain as it is.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: Pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Purchase new ambulance

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the Fire Chief to purchase a new 2023 Ford E350 4x2
Gasoline Powered Chassis, Cutaway Van for a not to exceed sum of $250,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: Avalon Fire Department has two (2) Road Rescue Ambulances  —  a 2000
Ford Diesel (Rescue 6) and 2005 Ford Diesel (Rescue 4).

Rescue 4 has had a series of mechanical issues, The engine has been rebuilt; however, issues
regarding the motor and electrical systems have persisted.

Fire personnel are working with Republic EVS in Santa Fe Springs to identify an appropriate
replacement for Rescue 4. As a part of the service agreement, Republic EVS will resell Rescue
4 to offset the cost of a new vehicle. At the time this report was authored, the approximate
resale value of Rescue 4 was undetermined.

Staff have received two quotes from Republic EVS:

 Vehicle Type  Price  Including Tax, Title and Fees
 2023 Ford E-350  $217,760.12  $239,643.39
 2024 Ford E-450  $240,882.51  $265,078.01

Fire Personnel has determined that the 2023 Ford E-350 is the most appropriate vehicle for
Avalon while also being the less expensive option.
  —

Both quotes contains a new battery powered gurney system Stryker Power-Pro Cot 6507,
  —

Stryker Power-Loader with Mass Casualty Fastener an approximately $74,188 additional
  —

cost. The City of Avalon is one of the few Fire Departments that does not currently utilize an
electronic or hydraulic powered gurney system. Currently, Fire Personnel manually lift patients
into and out of the ambulance. The upgraded electronic system has a 700 pound capacity and
will relieve Fire Personnel from the manual burden of lifting the gurney into the future
ambulance. The new system includes a 7 year service plan.

Since Fire Personnel have begun seeking quotes from qualified vendors, prices have increased
significantly. As such, Staff would like to lock in a rate as soon as possible. If authorized, the
City will not need to remit full payment until the ambulance is shipped to the Island  —an
 approximate 18-24 month lead time. However, the City will be responsible for making payment
on the gurney system within the current fiscal year $51,410.
  -

The current fiscal year budget has $250,000 for fire department vehicle replacement  —  fund
#10245-6871.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Approximately $52,000 to be expended as budgeted in Fiscal Year 2022-
23—fund #10245-6871.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Costs and wait times
will continue to rise and the Fire Department will not have a replacement vehicle for Rescue 4.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.
